chunks: Ahmad ibn Ziyad ibn Ja'far al-Hamadani (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: 'Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated to us, from Ja'far ibn Salama al-Ahwazi, from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Thaqafi. He said: Ahmad ibn 'Imran ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Layla al-Ansari narrated to us. He said: al-Hasan ibn 'Abdullah narrated to us, from Khalid ibn 'Isa al-Ansari, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla, who raises it [to the Prophet]. He said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him and his family) said:
The saints (siddiqun) are three: Habib al-Najjar, the believer of Al Yasin, who says:
'Follow the messengers; follow those who do not ask you for any reward, and who are rightly guided' (Quran 36:20-21)
and Hizqil, the believer of the Family of Pharaoh; and 'Ali ibn Abi Talib — and he is the best of them.

key_terms.الصِّدِّيقُونَ: Siddiqun — the utterly truthful, those of the highest rank of faith and sincerity; a Quranic title (4:69) designating those closest to the prophets in spiritual station
key_terms.رَفَعَهُ: Rafa'ahu — 'he raises it,' a technical hadith term indicating the chain is elevated to the Prophet without explicitly naming him at each step (mursal/marfu')
key_terms.مُؤْمِنُ آلِ فِرْعَوْنَ: The Believer of the Family of Pharaoh — Hizqil (Ezekiel/Hizkiah), the secret believer in Pharaoh's court (Quran 40:28)
key_terms.مُؤْمِنُ آلِ يَاسِينَ: The Believer of Al Yasin — Habib al-Najjar, who believed in the messengers sent to the city in Surah Ya-Sin (36:20)

ai.seo_question: Who are the three siddiqun (saints) mentioned in Islamic hadith tradition?
ai.summary: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) identified three individuals throughout history who earned the title 'siddiq' (the utterly truthful/saintly): Habib al-Najjar, a believer from the people to whom messengers were sent in Surah Ya-Sin; Hizqil, the unnamed believer from the court of Pharaoh mentioned in Surah Ghafir; and 'Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him), the first Imam, who is declared the best of the three. This hadith places 'Ali in the company of the most devout believers from prior prophetic missions, emphasizing his singular status in the Shia theological tradition as the greatest of the siddiqun.
word_analysis: may God have mercy on him

en.bilal-muhammad: Ahmad b. Ziyad b. Ja`far al-Hamadani (rh) narrated to us. He said: `Ali b. Ibrahim b. Hashim narrated to us from Ja`far b. Salama al-Ahwazi from Ibrahim b. Muhammad al-Thaqafi. He said: Ahmad b. `Imran b. Muhammad b. Abi Layla al-Ansari narrated to us. He said: Al-Husayn b. `Abdullah narrated to us from Khalid b. `Isa al-Ansari from `Abd al-Rahman b. Abi Layla, who raises it.

He said: The Messenger of Allah (s) said: There are three saints (siddiqun): (1) Habib al-Najjar, the believer of Al Yasin, who says, “Follow the messengers, follow those who are guided and do not ask you for reward” (36:20-21).
(2) Hizqil, the believer of the Family of Pharaoh. (3) `Ali b. Abi Talib, and he is the best of them.
